title: Design System: Huddle Web + Signal Handoff Landing

landingDirection.name: Signal Handoff

landingDirection.legacyRoutes: Keep the dark Neon Switchboard tokens until a later migration approval

components.description: A contained form, recordings, or dialog surface over the dot-grid canvas.
components.html:
MANAGED ROOM

narrative.overview:
Huddle is a dark operator surface for real-time work. The visual system should feel technical, cinematic, and controlled: a quiet violet-black room holds the meeting while Command Magenta and Consent Cyan behave like purposeful signals on a switchboard. The interface is expressive enough to feel like Huddle, but never so decorative that media, consent, recovery, or Host authority becomes harder to read.

Marketing surfaces may open the visual world with orbital imagery, dot lattices, and spacious type. Operative surfaces compress that same world into glass panels, concise status rails, clipped media tiles, and compact controls. Depth is layered and structural; neon is reserved for priority, focus, active state, and acknowledgement.

The system is intentionally dark-only. It rejects light themes, pastel SaaS styling, and generic rounded-card dashboards that would erase Huddle's operator character.
keyCharacteristics: Dark violet-black canvases with restrained magenta and cyan signal color.
Exo 2 gives headings and decisive actions geometric authority; Rajdhani keeps dense UI open and legible.
Frosted glass, hairline borders, and directional shadows organize layers without turning every panel into a floating card.
Cut-corner media frames and room-wide state rails make live content and authority visibly distinct.
Strong keyboard focus, visible system status, responsive call layouts, and reduced-motion fallbacks are part of the visual language.

rules.name: The One Signal per Moment Rule
rules.body: Command Magenta tells the user where authority or decisive action lives; Consent Cyan tells them what is active, approved, focused, or recoverable. Do not make both accents compete for the same action.

rules.name: The Dark Room Rule
rules.body: Huddle is dark-only. New surfaces inherit the Operator Background and create separation through tone, glass, hairlines, and light—not through white canvases.

rules.name: The Neon Budget Rule
rules.body: High-chroma accents occupy a small portion of a screen. Large fields stay neutral so video, text, and active system state remain readable.

rules.name: The Display Carries Authority Rule
rules.body: Exo 2 leads brand statements, decisions, and section ownership. Do not use it for long explanatory paragraphs.

rules.name: The Dense UI Stays Human Rule
rules.body: Rajdhani is the default for controls and supporting copy; do not compress important consent or error language into decorative uppercase labels.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: Monospace indicates identifiers, time, transport, or system state. It is not a general stylistic accent.

rules.name: The Media Owns the Stage Rule
rules.body: Controls, Host panels, status, and self-view must protect media rather than cover its most important regions.

rules.name: The Orientation Is the Contract Rule
rules.body: Portrait Equal Grid responds to viewport orientation, not user-agent, touch, or assumed device class.

rules.name: The Four Visible Rule
rules.body: In portrait Equal Grid, participant overflow scrolls after four visible rows; do not keep shrinking faces to avoid scrolling.

rules.name: The Structural First Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with tone, border, and placement before adding shadow.

rules.name: The Neon Must Be Earned Rule
rules.body: Glow appears because something is active, urgent, selected, or decisively actionable. A resting decorative card does not glow.

rules.name: The Overlay Casts Direction Rule
rules.body: Side panels cast inward; centered dialogs cast down and outward; status rails lift evenly. Shadow direction explains where the layer came from.

rules.name: The Cut Means Live Rule
rules.body: Cut-corner geometry belongs to video, screen-share, and Remote Control capture surfaces. Forms and ordinary cards stay gently rounded.

rules.name: The Round Means Immediate Rule
rules.body: Circular controls are for compact, direct in-call actions. Multi-step actions and text-heavy decisions use rounded rectangles or dialogs.

dos: Do preserve the dark-only Operator Background across every route and transient state.
Do use Command Magenta for decisive authority and Consent Cyan for focus, active state, approval, and recovery.
Do keep media unobscured, letterboxed with `object-contain`, and framed with the cut-corner live silhouette.
Do retain the Portrait Equal Grid contract: orientation-based, four visible rows, vertical overflow, existing gutters, and a floating local Self-view.
Do place Remote Control state below focused content and keep participant-scoped Request Control at the tile's bottom-right.
Do provide visible keyboard focus and remove nonessential animation under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do use the supplied Huddle mark and link every route-level logo or wordmark home.
donts: Don't introduce a light theme, pastel SaaS palette, or pale neutral dashboard surface.
Don't turn the product into a generic grid of interchangeable rounded cards; keep the dot-grid, glass hierarchy, signal color, and live-media geometry purposeful.
Don't spread neon across resting surfaces or let Command Magenta and Consent Cyan compete on the same action.
Don't crop camera faces or screen shares to fill a tile.
Don't overlay Host controls, Remote Control status, or self-view on critical shared-display content when layout space can hold them.
Don't use cut corners on ordinary forms, settings rows, or marketing cards.
Don't use monospace as decoration or compress consent, recovery, and error language into cryptic HUD copy.
